x: Len Fletcher's return to the field of racing was very pleasing, his position being identical with that in last year's race. Bert Webb took the prize for the first Belgrave in the scratch race without other award.

Our "B" team once again finished second in the Team Handicap and Len Fletcher, proving he can still show some of them the way round, finished fourteenth and was awarded the prize for the first unplaced member.

Young Dan Godfrey, many will remember his father, who was a walker in Len Fletcher's day, ran a good race in the 440 yards, but was unable to stave off the strong Wallington boy's finish in the last few yards.
Len Fletcher, one of our great walkers from 1925 onwards, is again in West Middlesex Hospital; but it is now hoped that a new course of treatment will bring almost complete recovery.
Regretfully we have to record the death of Len Fletcher, after a long illness, at the early age of 54 years. Our sincere condolences are extended to Mrs.

Len Fletcher and Frank Elson have assisted the Club in seven of these eight wins; Tommy Green six times; Fred Rickards on three occasions; Harold King, Frank Thorn and Ted Saunders each twice; and Joe King and Jack Field once each.

Len Fletcher says that if he asks for leave for walking ``The beaks of this Fred Karno outfit think you want to take a WAAF out''. Flight Sergeant Colin Sutton has hopped from the Middle East to India.
Len Fletcher and Colin Sutton each helped me along the hard road to taking part in what you describe, with great feeling, in your article "The Record Breaker".
